figures.finding: A resident pays a flat 20% personal income tax on Georgian-source income, with no tax-free allowance or regional layer; small-business status (turnover under GEL 500,000) gives a 1% rate on business income.
figures.applies: 2026; the Tax Code text (matsne.gov.ge) refused this environment ('Access Denied', 2026-11-01), so the rate is taken from PwC quoting it.

sources.said: Article 81 – Tax rate 1. A natural person's taxable income shall be taxed at the rate of 20%, unless otherwise provided for by this Code. ... Article 90 ... 1. Taxable income of a person having the status of a small business shall be taxed at 1% ... 2. ... at 3% if his/her gross income ... has exceeded GEL 500 000

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; a return is due before 1 April of the next year from those whose income was not taxed at source; an entrepreneur pays estimated tax in four instalments (15 May, 15 July, 15 September, 15 December).
figures.applies: Individuals. The Georgian text's 1 აპრილამდე is before 1 April: the return's last day is 31 March.

sources.said: Article 135 – Accounting period 1. The accounting period for a person ... shall be a calendar year. ... Article 155 – Current taxes ... a) not later than 15 May – 25%; b) not later than 15 July – 25%; c) by not later than 15 September – 25%; d) by not later than 15 December – 25%. ... An income tax/profit tax return shall be filed with a tax authority by 1 April of a year following the reporting year by: a) resident natural persons whose income is not taxed at a Georgian source

figures.finding: Georgia has no social security contributions; the funded pension takes 2% of salary from the employee and 2% from the employer (a self-employed person pays 4%), and the state adds 2% (to GEL 24,000) or 1% (GEL 24,000 to 60,000).
figures.applies: 2026; pension participation is mandatory for employees, voluntary for the self-employed.

sources.said: a) an employer shall ... in favour of an employee, transfer ... in the amount of 2% of the taxable salary paid to the employee within the accounting period ... b) an employer shall ... on behalf and at the expense of an employee, transfer ... in the amount of 2% of the taxable salary ... d) a self-employed person shall ... in the amount of 4% of the income of the self-employed person ... e) the State shall make a pension contribution ...: e.a) within the first GEL 24 000 of the annual salary/annual income ... in the amount of 2% ...; e.b) ... from the said amount to GEL 60 000 inclusive, in the amount of 1% ...; f) the state shall not make a pension contribution on the taxable salary ... over GEL 60 000

figures.finding: Salary is taxed at the source of payment (the 20% rate); only those whose income was not taxed at source file a return.
figures.applies: Employment income paid by a Georgian payer.

sources.said: Tax shall be withheld at source by a tax agent who is a legal person, an enterprise/organisation or entrepreneur natural person, namely: a) a person paying salary to an employee

figures.finding: A freelancer's fee bears 18% VAT once taxable turnover exceeds GEL 100,000 in any continuous 12 months.

sources.said: Article 166 – VAT rate The VAT rate shall be 18%.

figures.finding: A non-resident's income from services rendered in Georgia, not through a permanent establishment, bears 10% withholding (stated for non-resident enterprises; royalties 5%).
figures.applies: Non-resident payees without a PE; the individual performer's rate under Article 17 terms was not found stated separately. Article 134 states the rates for every non-resident, not only enterprises.

sources.said: b 1 ) royalty – 5%; ... e) other paid amounts, which under this Code are regarded as Georgian source income – at the rate of 10%; f) salary income – at the rate fixed by Article 81 of this Code. 1 1 . Income earned by a person registered in a country with a preferential tax treatment in cases provided for in paragraph 1(b), (b 1 ) and (e) of this article shall be taxed at source without deductions, at 15%.

figures.finding: A non-resident individual's fee for work in Georgia, not tied to a permanent establishment there, is taxed at source at 10% of the gross with no deductions; that is the tax, unless the non-resident files a return by 1 April of the next year for a recalculation, which can only lower it.

value.final: yes, unless a return is filed by 1 April of the next year for recalculation and refund (art. 134(3)-(4))

figures.applies: Non-resident individuals' fees for services (a performer's, a director's, a producer's); salary is taxed at the art. 81 rate

sources.said: Art. 80(3): "The gross income of a non-resident natural person that is not related to his/her permanent establishment in Georgia shall be taxed under Article 134 of this Code at source without deductions". Art. 134(1): "Income earned by a non-resident from a Georgian-based source shall be taxed at the source without deductions at the following rates: ... (e) other paid amounts, which under this Code are regarded as Georgian source income – at the rate of 10%. (f) salary income – at the rate fixed by Article 81". (3): "A non-resident who earns income under paragraph 1(c)-(e) of this article and is taxed at the source, may file a return by the 1 April of the year following the reporting year requesting recalculation and refund of withheld taxes." (4)(c): "taxes paid by a non-resident shall not exceed the amount withheld at the source".

sources.title: Legislative Herald of Georgia (matsne.gov.ge): Tax Code of Georgia, consolidated English text, arts. 154 and 165
sources.said: Article 154 – Procedure for withholding tax at source 1. Tax shall be withheld at source by a tax agent who is a legal person, an enterprise/organisation or entrepreneur natural person, namely: a) a person paying salary to an employee ... Article 165 – Registration as a VAT taxpayer 1. A taxable person shall, unless otherwise provided for by this Code, from the day when he/she exceeds the total amount of GEL 100 000 for VAT taxable transactions of supplying goods/providing services carried out during any 12 consecutive calendar months, within not later than 2 business days, apply to a tax authority for registration as a VAT taxpayer.
